deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page continues the section 'Der physische Raum als Lichtmedium'. Riemann adopts the simplest (Fresnel-type) hypothesis for light: a ray is a propagating motion in which all ether particles lying in a plane normal to the ray keep their relative positions and oscillate together within that plane, never leaving it.

(a) Constancy of density. Consider an elementary cylinder whose axis lies along the propagation direction and whose two end faces lie in two planes normal to it. Each end face moves rigidly within its own plane, so the cylinder's length and cross-section are unchanged and its volume is preserved. Hence the ether density is unaltered. In modern terms, a displacement u = (0, u_y(x,t), u_z(x,t)) has div u = 0. Riemann's argument is geometric, not written as a formula.

(b) Empirical input. The propagation speed c is the same for all rays and all colours (no dispersion in vacuo).

(c) Kinematic set-up. Let x,y,z be coordinates of fixed geometric space points. Let xi,eta,zeta be coordinates of the physical (ether) point that oscillates about (x,y,z) at time t. Let x1',y1',z1' be the particle velocities. The right-margin block expresses one set of coordinates as functions of the other and of t, and t-derivatives give the velocities: x1' = dx/dt etc. are functions of (xi,eta,zeta,t). By inverting the map, they are therefore also functions of (x,y,z,t). This licenses treating the velocities as fields on geometric space, i.e. passing from a Lagrangian to an Eulerian description. The step is valid for small oscillations; this justification is my addition.

(d) Plane wave along the x-axis. Riemann characterises the wave by saying that the motion at geometric point x at time T equals the motion at x+ct at time T-t, and also the motion at x-ct at time T+t. He writes the integrated velocity, i.e. the displacement, as
  int x1' dt = f(x+ct) + f1(x-ct)  (d'Alembert's general solution).
He then states the field equations for a wave along x:
  x1' = 0 (transversality: no longitudinal motion);
  c^2 d^2 y1'/dx^2 = d^2 y1'/dt^2;
  c^2 d^2 z1'/dx^2 = d^2 z1'/dt^2.

(e) Preparing the 3-D form. Particles in a plane x = const keep their relative positions. So the velocity field does not depend on y,z, and d^2/dy^2 = d^2/dz^2 = 0 (a struck attempt writes this with dy/dy, dz/dz). The equations can therefore be written 'more symmetrically' as d^2 v/dt^2 = c^2 (v_xx + v_yy + v_zz) for each component. This form appears on the next page, which then uses rotation invariance of the Laplacian and superposition to extend it to arbitrary directions and many waves.
errors: The verbal characterisation in (d) is internally redundant. u(x,T) = u(x+ct, T-t) for all t forces u = F(x+cT). u(x,T) = u(x-ct, T+t) for all t also forces u = F(x+cT), since x-ct+c(T+t) = x+cT. So both conditions describe only a wave travelling toward -x. They do not yield the two-term solution f(x+ct)+f1(x-ct) written immediately afterwards. Presumably one sign pair was intended reversed, or the sum of two oppositely travelling waves was meant.

The formula int x1' dt = f(x+ct)+f1(x-ct) is written for x1', yet the next line sets x1' = 0 (the longitudinal component). The d'Alembert form should refer to the transverse components y1', z1', or to a generic component.

Notation is inconsistent. The text says xi,eta,zeta are the particle coordinates attached to geometric point (x,y,z), i.e. xi = xi(x,y,z,t). The margin writes x = (xi,eta,zeta,t) and calls dx/dt the velocity. The next page's struck column reverts to xi = (x,y,z,t). The roles are interchanged in the margin.

The identification of the Lagrangian velocity d xi/dt with an Eulerian field satisfying the wave equation in the geometric coordinates is tacitly a small-amplitude (linearised) approximation; this is not stated.

The incompressibility claim holds for a single transverse plane wave. For superposed waves in different directions, the next page's equation for each component does not by itself enforce div = 0, and Riemann does not impose a transversality condition there.

results.what: Ether density is unchanged under transverse plane-wave motion (elementary-cylinder argument), equivalent to div u = 0 for u = (0, u_y(x,t), u_z(x,t))
results.modern_name: Transversality / incompressibility of transverse plane waves
results.usually_credited_to: Fresnel (transverse light waves, c. 1821); Cauchy and Green (elastic ether theories, 1830s)

results.what: Displacement along the propagation axis is f(x+ct)+f1(x-ct); each transverse component satisfies c^2 u_xx = u_tt
Use of the colour-independence of c and the passage from Lagrangian to Eulerian velocity fields, preparing the 3-D wave equation u_tt = c^2 Laplacian(u)
results.modern_name: Vector wave equation for a non-dispersive elastic ether

deep.surprise_reason: This is standard early-19th-century elastic-ether optics (Fresnel transversality, d'Alembert solution, the wave equation), written in a didactic, heavily corrected style. It may be lecture or study notes. Nothing goes beyond textbook material of the period. The only point of interest is documentary: it records Riemann's (or his source's) kinematic set-up for the ether.

checkable.sympy: x,t,c=symbols('x t c'); f,g=Function('f'),Function('g'); u=f(x+c*t)+g(x-c*t); simplify(diff(u,t,2)-c**2*diff(u,x,2))==0
checkable.asserts: The d'Alembert form satisfies the 1-D wave equation c^2 u_xx = u_tt.

checkable.sympy: x,T,t,c=symbols('x T t c'); F=Function('F'); u=lambda X,TT: F(X+c*TT); simplify(u(x+c*t,T-t)-u(x,T))==0 and simplify(u(x-c*t,T+t)-u(x,T))==0
checkable.asserts: Both of Riemann's stated conditions are satisfied by the single wave F(x+cT), i.e. they are the same condition.

checkable.sympy: x,T,t,c=symbols('x T t c'); G=Function('G'); u=lambda X,TT: G(X-c*TT); simplify(u(x+c*t,T-t)-u(x,T))==0
checkable.asserts: Evaluates to False: a wave moving toward +x does not satisfy the first stated condition, confirming the conditions capture only one direction.

checkable.sympy: x,y,z,t,c=symbols('x y z t c'); f,g=Function('f'),Function('g'); U=Matrix([0,f(x-c*t),g(x-c*t)]); diff(U[0],x)+diff(U[1],y)+diff(U[2],z)==0
checkable.asserts: A transverse plane wave along x is divergence-free, so the ether density is unchanged (the cylinder argument).

checkable.sympy: x,y,z,t,c=symbols('x y z t c'); g=Function('g'); v=g(x-c*t); simplify(diff(v,t,2)-c**2*(diff(v,x,2)+diff(v,y,2)+diff(v,z,2)))==0
checkable.asserts: If the field is independent of y,z, the 1-D equation equals the symmetric 3-D form u_tt = c^2 Laplacian(u) of the next page.

checkable.sympy: x,y,z,th=symbols('x y z theta'); f=Function('f'); X=x*cos(th)-y*sin(th); Y=x*sin(th)+y*cos(th); h=f(X,Y,z); L=diff(h,x,2)+diff(h,y,2)+diff(h,z,2); simplify(L.doit())
checkable.asserts: Rotation invariance of the Laplacian, used on the next page to carry the equations to waves in other directions; the result should equal the Laplacian in the rotated variables.

transcription_corrections: Line 'für alle Lichtstrahlen auch x der verschiedenen Farben': the 'x' appears to be an insertion/reference mark rather than part of the text, and 'dieselbe ist' has been moved up into the first line as an insertion. Read: 'Die Erfahrung zeigt dass die Geschwindigkeit (c) der Fortpflanzung d. Bewegungsform für alle Lichtstrahlen auch der verschiedenen Farben dieselbe ist.'

The right-margin insertion beside the struck 'physischen Raumpunktes' reads '+ [Wenn, struck] Bezeichnet man', keyed by the cross/plus mark to the start of the next line, rather than 'x Bezeichnet man'.
'der Coordinaten der physischen Raumes': likely 'des physischen Raumes' or 'des physischen Raumpunktes' (insertion above the struck 'des Stofftheilchens').
'{+ab+}' after 'geometrischen Raumpunkte' is doubtful and may be an insertion mark or a fragment; the intended reading is simply 'die Coordinaten der geometrischen Raumpunkte'.

In 'int x1' dt = f(x+ct)+f1(x-ct)', the integrand is written with the same symbol as the velocity; the image supports x1' (or possibly a generic component). The struck preceding version reads '(x = f(x+ct)+f1(x-ct))'.
'der sich zur Zeit t um den Punkt (x,y,z) schwingt': the image suggests 'der zur Zeit t um den Punkt (x,y,z) schwingt', with 'sich' possibly absent or struck.
